findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category site setting row is absent
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. Site settings are only persisted to the site_settings table once changed from their default, so on most installs (where embed_category was never set) the query returns no rows and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError and failing the migration for everyone. Same problem on line 15 for the uncategorized_category_id lookup. Both lookups need nil-safe handling (e.g. use `SiteSetting` defaults or guard against empty results).

findings.title: Host values interpolated directly into INSERT SQL
findings.body: The migration builds `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` by string interpolation. The embeddable_hosts setting was free-form text, so any line containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) will break the migration or inject unintended SQL. Values should be quoted/escaped (e.g. via `quote_value` or ActiveRecord inserts).

findings.title: create_table with force: true and irreversible data migration inside change
findings.body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will silently drop an existing embeddable_hosts table (data loss if the migration is ever re-run against a partially migrated database). Additionally, the data copy and the `DELETE FROM site_settings` make the migration effectively irreversible while living in a `change` method, so `rake db:rollback` will fail or destroy the old settings with no way back.

findings.title: update/destroy crash with 500 when host id does not exist
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown/stale id, then `save_host(host)` calls `host.host = ...` and `host.destroy` on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of a 404. Should render not_found when the record is missing.

findings.title: before_validation calls sub! on possibly-nil host
findings.body: The `before_validation` block runs `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If a request creates/updates a host without a `host` parameter (params[:embeddable_host][:host] is nil or the key is missing), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. It should guard with `if self.host.present?` so the format validation can report the error properly.

findings.title: Host validation regex too restrictive
findings.body: The format regex requires a dot and a 2–5 letter TLD (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`), so valid hosts like `localhost:3000`, `my_host.example.com` (underscore), hosts with new long TLDs, or trailing dots are rejected. Since this list drives which sites can embed comments, admins on intranet/dev setups will be unable to configure valid hosts and will get only a generic format error.

findings.title: update action is a no-op
findings.body: PUT /admin/customize/embedding simply re-serializes the current state and ignores the request body entirely, while the new admin UI's `saveChanges` action calls `embedding.update({})` as if it persisted something. The endpoint silently discards any submitted changes; either implement the update or remove the save control so admins are not misled into thinking embedding settings were saved.

findings.title: Fabricator contents swapped between files
findings.body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. The files' contents are exchanged. It happens to work because fabricators are loaded globally, but every future edit (e.g. someone adding a category fabricator to the 'right' file or deleting what looks like a duplicate) will be error-prone; the contents should be in their correctly named files.

findings.title: No index on embeddable_hosts.host despite per-request lookup
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` on every `/embed/comments` and `/embed/count` request (these are high-traffic, cacheable embed endpoints hit by every page view of embedding sites). There is no index on `host`, so each embed request triggers a full table scan once more than a handful of hosts exist. Add an index (on `lower(host)` for Postgres) in the migration.

findings.title: New hosts saved without a category send null and lose user's choice context
findings.body: For a newly added host, `categoryId` is initialized to null and the category-chooser starts empty; save sends `category_id: null`, which the server silently converts to the uncategorized category. Combined with `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checking host presence and `TopicEmbed.import` using the host's category for new topics, hosts accidentally created without a category will post embedded topics to Uncategorized with no warning. Also, `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))` returns undefined for a null category, leaving `host.category` unset after save until reload.

findings.title: No request specs for new admin controllers
findings.body: Both new controller specs only assert the controller's superclass. There are no tests for create/update/destroy of embeddable hosts (including the nil-host-param crash, blank category fallback to uncategorized, and validation error rendering) or for the embedding show/update endpoints. Given this PR replaces a working site-setting mechanism with new endpoints and a data migration, the behavior is essentially untested.

findings.title: expandable_first_post? no longer requires any embeddable host
findings.body: The check `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && ...` was reduced to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. A stale TopicEmbed with no matching EmbeddableHost (e.g. after the host was deleted, which nothing prevents) will still be treated as expandable, triggering `TopicEmbed.expanded_for` remote fetches for hosts that are no longer allowed. If the host requirement was intentionally dropped, the migration should also clean up orphaned topic_embeds or the retrieval should be validated against EmbeddableHost.
